Calculate dysbiosis scores

Source: R/AllGenerics.R, R/addDysbiosis.R
addDysbiosis.Rd

Dysbiosis scores measure how much the community of a sample differs from the communities of control samples.

addDysbiosis(x, ...)

getDysbiosis(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
addDysbiosis(x, ...)

# S4 method for class 'SummarizedExperiment'
getDysbiosis(
  x,
  col.var,
  assay.type = "counts",
  index = "median_distance",
  name = index,
  method = "bray",
  ...
)

Arguments

x

a SummarizedExperiment object.

...

Additional arguments. The following optional arguments are supported:

  • reference: NULL or Character scalar. Specifies the group in col.var that is used as controls. If NULL, the first level of factor(x[[col.var]]) is used. (Default: NULL)

  • group: NULL or Character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) (e.g., subject ID). Control samples that share the same value with the current sample are excluded from its comparison. (Default: NULL)

  • k: Integer scalar. Number of nearest control samples used by cloud. (Default: 5% of the control samples, at least 1)

  • altexp: NULL or Character scalar. If provided, use this altExp assay container of x for the computation. (Default: NULL)

  • Further arguments are passed to getDissimilarity.

col.var

Character scalar. Specifies a variable from colData(x) that defines the groups.

assay.type

Character scalar. Specifies the name of assay used in calculation. (Default: "counts")

index

Character vector. Specifies the dysbiosis scores to calculate. (Default: "median_distance")

name

Character vector. Specifies the column names for the scores in colData(x). (Default: index)

method

Character scalar. Specifies the dissimilarity measure passed to getDissimilarity. (Default: "bray")

Value

getDysbiosis returns a DataFrame with one row per sample. addDysbiosis returns x with the scores added to colData(x).

Details

The following scores are available:

  • median_distance: Median dissimilarity between the sample and the control samples. The sample itself is excluded from the controls. With Bray-Curtis dissimilarity, this is the dysbiosis score of Lloyd-Price et al. (2019).

  • centroid_distance: Distance from the sample to the centroid of the control samples minus its distance to the centroid of the other samples (AlShawaqfeh et al. 2017). Positive values mean that the sample is closer to the other samples than to the controls. Centroids are computed from the dissimilarities, and each sample is included in the centroid of its own group.

  • shannon_jsd: Mean difference in Shannon diversity between the sample and the control samples, multiplied by its mean Jensen-Shannon divergence to them (Santiago et al. 2019). The sample itself is excluded from the controls. method is not used.

  • reference_plane: Euclidean distance, in the first three principal coordinates of the dissimilarities, from the sample to a plane fitted to the control samples and restricted to their range (Halfvarson et al. 2017).

  • cloud: CLOUD statistic (Montassier et al. 2018): the mean dissimilarity from the sample to its k nearest control samples, divided by the same quantity averaged over the control samples (each compared with the other controls). Values above 1 mean that the sample is further from the controls than controls are from each other.

The centroid_distance, shannon_jsd and reference_plane scores are adapted from the dysbiosisR package (Shetty and de Steenhuijsen Piters).

getDissimilarity, addDivergence

Examples

data(Tengeler2020)
tse <- Tengeler2020

tse <- addDysbiosis(tse, col.var = "patient_status", reference = "Control")
colData(tse)[, c("patient_status", "median_distance")]
#> DataFrame with 27 rows and 2 columns
#>      patient_status median_distance
#>         <character>       <numeric>
#> A110           ADHD        0.861712
#> A111        Control        0.749701
#> A12            ADHD        0.887248
#> A13         Control        0.745962
#> A14         Control        0.764283
#> ...             ...             ...
#> A35         Control        0.615141
#> A36            ADHD        0.724467
#> A37            ADHD        0.721312
#> A38         Control        0.614832
#> A39            ADHD        0.742831

# Other scores
res <- getDysbiosis(
    tse, col.var = "patient_status", reference = "Control",
    index = c("centroid_distance", "reference_plane", "cloud"))
head(res)
#> DataFrame with 6 rows and 3 columns
#>      centroid_distance reference_plane     cloud
#>              <numeric>       <numeric> <numeric>
#> A110         0.1943507       0.2894502   1.84539
#> A111        -0.1511192       0.1120120   1.26796
#> A12          0.2069464       0.5824895   2.63572
#> A13         -0.0768137       0.0222043   1.26796
#> A14         -0.0838556       0.0859448   1.06469
#> A15          0.1120201       0.3821137   1.88400
